record.context_brief: condition number for model-space shift compression
record.original_question: Let Theta be a finite Blaschke product with distinct zeros, and let S_Theta be the compression of the unilateral shift to the model space K_Theta associated with Theta. For a matrix representing S_Theta that is diagonalized as A = X D X^{-1}, what is the smallest possible condition number ||X|| ||X^{-1}|| among eigenvector matrices X?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Theta$ be a finite Blaschke product with $n$ distinct zeros, namely
$$\Theta(z) \;=\; \prod_{j=1}^{n} \frac{z-\lambda_j}{1-\overline{\lambda_j}z}, \qquad \lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n \in \mathbb{D} \text{ distinct},$$
and let $K_\Theta = H^2 \ominus \Theta H^2$ denote the associated model space inside the Hardy space $H^2$ of the open unit disk $\mathbb{D}$. Let $S \colon H^2 \to H^2$ be the unilateral shift $(Sf)(z)=zf(z)$, and let
$$S_\Theta \;=\; P_{K_\Theta} S\big|_{K_\Theta}$$
be the compression of $S$ to $K_\Theta$, where $P_{K_\Theta}$ is the orthogonal projection onto $K_\Theta$. The operator $S_\Theta$ acts on the $n$-dimensional space $K_\Theta$ and its spectrum is $\{\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n\}$; in particular it is diagonalizable, so for any matrix representation $A$ of $S_\Theta$ in an orthonormal basis of $K_\Theta$ there exists an invertible $X \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ and a diagonal $D \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ with $A = X D X^{-1}$.

Determine, as a function of the zeros $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n$, the minimal possible value of the condition number
$$\kappa(X) \;=\; \|X\|\,\|X^{-1}\|$$
(with respect to the spectral / operator $2$-norm) over all such eigenvector matrices $X$ diagonalizing $S_\Theta$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is explicitly listed as an open problem in a recent compilation of open problems in function-theoretic operator theory. No published solution determining the minimal eigenvector-matrix condition number of the compressed shift $S_\Theta$ on a model space with a finite Blaschke product symbol could be located.
